approach: Add an `athena.focus/1` record (id, n, at, text, set_by) at records/focus/<month>/<id>.json. `Records.focus` loads it, and the record with the greatest `n` is the current focus. `Athena::set_focus` and `current_focus` back `athena focus [text]`, and `StatusView.focus` makes `athena status` print it. Add `[priority_caps]` (urgent = 3, high = 10) to the schema and to athena.toml. The cap is applied to each planned item's OWN priority (the request or person level), not the dependency-raised one, as the critic proposed. `Plan::build_capped(entries, history, &PriorityCaps)` works in four steps. (1) It builds the uncapped plan and uses its order as the plan order. (2) It runs the urgent cap and then the high cap over the own priorities. An item with a person priority record at the capped tier is kept and counts toward the cap; the other slots go to the rest in uncapped plan order; the excess drops one tier, and an item pushed out of urgent into high takes part in the high pass. (3) It rebuilds the plan from the capped own priorities, so the existing raising logic lifts the prerequisites of kept items by itself. (4) It records one `Demotion` for each item whose final effective tier is lower than its uncapped effective tier. `priority_violations` uses the same capped own priorities. `Drain::prepare` (shared by `athena plan` and `drain`) gets the caps from a new defaulted `Steps::priority_caps`, which `RealSteps` fills from `JobConfig::at` and the priority records. `display::plan` prints one `demoted` line per demotion. Planning writes nothing. Binary-level tests set up queued requests by writing records straight into the fixture, as tests/drain.rs does.

decisions.choice: Cap the own priority (entry.priority, or the person's record level), then rerun the existing raising logic on the capped vector. Record a Demotion only when an item's final effective tier is lower than its uncapped effective tier. Answers finding 2.
decisions.reason: effective_priorities raises every prerequisite to its dependent's tier. Counting those raised prerequisites as separate picks lets older prerequisites push out the urgent dependent that raised them. Capping own levels counts only items someone asked to be urgent. A kept dependent raises its prerequisites back by itself, and a demoted dependent no longer raises them. So no closure rule or level filter is needed. Raised prerequisites are not counted against the cap; the docs and CHANGELOG say so.

rejected.option: Cap the dependency-raised tiers with a closure rule (previous Decisions 1, 3 and 4)
rejected.why: The fill by (rung, age) keeps older prerequisites and demotes the urgent dependent that caused them to count.

rejected.option: Add a priority_set_at field to PlanEntry
rejected.why: About 12 PlanEntry literals in drain.rs, tests/drain.rs and plan.rs would need edits. A side set in PriorityCaps avoids that.

decisions.choice: The cap works through a private build_inner(entries, history, overrides: &BTreeMap<String, Priority>). build_with calls it with no overrides. Plan gains `demoted: Vec<Demotion>` (skipped in JSON when empty) and a `#[serde(skip)]` map of the capped own priorities. effective_priorities takes the own priorities as an argument. priority_violations reads them from the Plan.
decisions.reason: The ordering and grouping code stays in one place. The existing wave logic needs no copy. priority_violations judges the order by the same tiers the plan used, so a demotion cannot show up as a contradiction. Entries are never mutated.

rejected.option: Lower entry.priority on cloned entries before build_with
rejected.why: The Plan could not report the uncapped tiers, and priority_violations would need the clones.

decisions.choice: Person-set means the job has a priority record. PriorityCaps.person_set is a BTreeSet<String> of job ids, built from the jobs' priorities. In a capped tier, the items in the set whose own level is that tier are kept even if they alone exceed the cap. The remaining slots go to the other items, in uncapped plan order, up to the cap.
decisions.reason: The accepted reading says a person's priority record still wins for its item and the item is never demoted below it. That rule, not a ranking, decides who is kept. 'Most recent first' therefore needs no tiebreak, because every person-set item in the tier is kept. This is stated in the help text and CHANGELOG, and left as an open question for the owner.

rejected.option: Demote the oldest person-set items when they exceed the cap
rejected.why: It contradicts the accepted reading, and the 'person record wins' test could not fail.

decisions.choice: The focus record is `{id: RecordId, n: u32 (from 1), at, text, set_by}`. The current focus is the one with the greatest n; set_focus uses max(n)+1. The path is records/focus/<month>/<id>.json, the same shape as Intervention (id.month(), id). set_by comes from git user.name, and set_focus refuses an empty text or an empty identity. Answers finding 3.
decisions.reason: PriorityRecord already orders itself with an explicit n. Using the random id suffix as a counter would give it a meaning no other record uses. The criterion 2 test then does not depend on how ids are minted or on the second.

rejected.option: Use RecordId::from_parts(at, n) and order by id
rejected.why: The suffix is 20 random bits, not a sequence.
It is not reliably set or recorded.

decisions.choice: Pass caps and the person-set through a new defaulted trait method `Steps::priority_caps(&self) -> PriorityCaps` (default: no caps). RealSteps overrides it with `JobConfig::at(&self.athena.git, &self.athena.head()?)` for `config.priority_caps`, and `self.records()` for the person-set. Answers finding 1.
decisions.reason: The only production caller is Drain::prepare (Plan::build_with at drain.rs:2008), shared by `athena plan` and `drain`. Config and records reach it only through Steps. A default keeps every fake Steps impl compiling. drain.rs is outside the listed deliverables but has no substitute. The summary will name it as a required extra file.

rejected.why: It forces edits to the fake impls in tests/drain.rs and elsewhere.

rejected.option: Skip drain.rs and cap only inside `athena plan` display
rejected.why: The drain would still work in the uncapped order, so the cap would not govern the work.

decisions.choice: Name the section `[priority_caps]` with `urgent = 3` and `high = 10`, as a #[serde(default)] struct with deny_unknown_fields. Reset it in Config::reading_inputs.
decisions.reason: Matches how [parallel] works: older configs still parse and readings' config digest does not change.

decisions.choice: Cascade the high pass: items demoted out of urgent count in the high tier, and the excess there drops to normal. One Demotion per item records its final from and to, so one line per item.
decisions.reason: The reading says demoted items count toward the high cap. The request says one line per demoted item.

rejected.option: Demote each item at most one tier, letting high exceed 10

decisions.choice: Set up the binary-level test data by writing Request and Priority records directly into the Fixture repo (commit_records_to style, tests/drain.rs:4605), then run the real `athena plan` binary. Answers finding 4.
decisions.reason: This is a proven setup, and it avoids relying on the unchecked assumption that `ask --later` text yields a complete entry. The test first asserts that all 5 ids appear in the plan order, so an incomplete entry fails loudly.

rejected.why: Whether it yields a complete entry without a model call was never checked.

decisions.choice: No refusal_corpus case is added, and `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` is not made a demonstration. Answers finding 5 as well: the open question about the records gate is dropped.

Records::load discovery is covered by step 5.

open_questions: The accepted reading says a person's priority record is never demoted, so items set by hand are kept even when they alone exceed a cap. The motivating case (13 urgent items set by hand) would then not shrink. If the owner meant the cap to bind person-set items too (oldest-set demoted first), the reading must be revised. The plan implements the reading as accepted.
drain.rs is outside the listed deliverables but has no substitute for the wiring. If the scope check refuses it, the caps cannot reach `athena plan`.

Will request records written into the fixture with a bullet and plain wording give complete plan entries, with a goal, a rung that infer_rung derives and acceptance? infer_rung was not read. The test asserts all 5 ids are planned before the cap assertions, and the producer fits the wording.

Raised prerequisites are not counted against a cap, so the effective urgent tier can hold more than 3 items when a kept urgent item depends on others. This follows the critic's fix; the docs and CHANGELOG will say it.
An urgent item pushed out of the high tier lands at normal, two tiers down, with one merged line. This follows the reading that demoted items count toward the high cap.
